subject: pe
question: 屈肘動作由肱二頭肌與肱三頭肌共同參與。試說明兩者在此動作中的角色，並解釋何以肌肉只能拉不能推。
questionEn: Flexing the elbow involves both the biceps and the triceps. State the role of each in this movement, and explain why muscle can only pull and not push.
explanation: 本題考核主動肌與拮抗肌的概念。答卷須指出兩者角色相反而非同時收縮，並由肌肉的構造解釋只能拉的原因。
explanationEn: This tests the concepts of agonist and antagonist. The answer must show that the two have opposite roles rather than contracting together, and explain the pull-only property from muscle structure.
referenceAnswer:
兩者的角色：
肱二頭肌為主動肌（作用肌）。屈肘時它向心收縮，肌肉長度縮短，把前臂拉向上臂。
肱三頭肌為拮抗肌。同一動作中它舒張並受控地伸長，容許關節活動；若它同時強力收縮，肘關節會僵住而無法屈曲。
兩者構成拮抗肌對：伸肘時角色對調，肱三頭肌成為主動肌，肱二頭肌成為拮抗肌。
何以肌肉只能拉不能推：
肌肉的收縮單位為肌小節，其中肌動蛋白細絲與肌凝蛋白粗絲互相重疊。收縮時橫橋擺動，把細絲拉向肌小節中央，令肌小節縮短。整個過程只能產生【縮短】方向的力，因為橫橋只能拉，不能把細絲推開。
結果是肌肉只能把兩端的骨骼拉近，不能把它們推開。故每一個關節動作都需要至少兩組方向相反的肌肉：一組負責屈，另一組負責伸。
此一限制解釋了為何身體各處的肌肉都成對出現 —— 若肌肉能推，拮抗肌便不必要。
referenceAnswerEn:
Roles: the biceps is the agonist. In flexion it contracts concentrically, shortens, and draws the forearm towards the upper arm. The triceps is the antagonist: in the same movement it relaxes and lengthens under control so that the joint can move; were it to contract strongly at the same time the elbow would lock and could not flex. The two form an antagonistic pair, and in extension the roles reverse.
Why muscle can only pull: the contractile unit is the sarcomere, in which thin actin filaments overlap thick myosin filaments. During contraction the cross-bridges swing and draw the thin filaments towards the centre of the sarcomere, shortening it. The process can generate force only in the shortening direction, because a cross-bridge can pull but cannot push the filaments apart.
The consequence is that a muscle can only draw the bones at its two ends closer together, never push them apart. Every joint movement therefore requires at least two opposing muscle groups, one to flex and one to extend.
This limitation explains why muscles throughout the body occur in pairs: if muscle could push, antagonists would be unnecessary.

subject: pe
question: 熱身運動一般分為一般性熱身與專項熱身兩部分。試說明兩者的目的差異，並指出只做一般性熱身的不足。
questionEn: A warm-up usually has a general phase and a specific phase. Explain how their purposes differ, and state what is missing if only the general phase is done.
explanation: 本題須指出兩個階段服務不同目標，而非只答「熱身可防受傷」。不足一問要扣連專項動作的特性。
explanationEn: The answer must show that the two phases serve different objectives rather than state that warming up prevents injury, and the shortfall must relate to the demands of the specific activity.
referenceAnswer:
一般性熱身的目的：
提升核心體溫與肌肉溫度，加快代謝反應速率；增加心率與血流量，使更多血液輸往工作肌；降低肌肉與結締組織的黏滯性，令組織較易伸展；並提高神經傳導速度。做法多為慢跑、踏步等全身性低強度活動。
專項熱身的目的：
以接近比賽動作的形式，預先激活即將使用的肌群與動作模式。例如短跑選手做高抬腿與加速跑，投擲項目做漸進式揮臂。目的在於神經肌肉的協調：讓中樞神經預先「排練」該動作的徵召次序與時序，同時把關節活動範圍推展至比賽所需的幅度。
只做一般性熱身的不足：
一、體溫雖已提升，但即將使用的動作模式未經激活。動作愈複雜、速度愈快、幅度愈大，此一缺口愈明顯。
二、關節未在比賽所需的角度與速度下活動過。例如網球發球需要肩關節作大幅度外旋，慢跑無法提供此一準備，首個發球即以最大幅度進行，受傷風險上升。
三、運動表現亦受影響。神經肌肉協調未經預熱，初段的動作效率與準確度較低。
故專項熱身不可由延長一般性熱身取代 —— 兩者處理的是不同的系統：前者是循環與代謝，後者是神經肌肉。
referenceAnswerEn:
Purpose of the general phase: to raise core and muscle temperature and so the rate of metabolic reactions; to increase heart rate and blood flow so that more blood reaches the working muscles; to reduce the viscosity of muscle and connective tissue so that they extend more readily; and to raise nerve conduction velocity. It is usually whole-body low-intensity work such as jogging or stepping.
Purpose of the specific phase: to pre-activate the muscle groups and movement patterns about to be used, in a form close to the competitive action — high knees and build-up runs for a sprinter, progressive arm swings for a thrower. The aim is neuromuscular co-ordination: the central nervous system rehearses the recruitment order and timing of the movement, while the joints are taken through the range the event requires.
What is missing with only the general phase: temperature has risen but the movement pattern to be used has not been activated, and the gap widens as the action becomes more complex, faster and larger in range. The joints have not moved at the angles and speeds competition demands — a tennis serve needs large external rotation at the shoulder, which jogging does not prepare, so the first serve is taken at full range with raised risk of injury. Performance also suffers, since without neuromuscular preparation the efficiency and accuracy of early movements are lower.
The specific phase therefore cannot be replaced by a longer general phase: they address different systems, circulation and metabolism on the one hand, the neuromuscular system on the other.

subject: pe
question: 最大攝氧量（VO₂max）常被用作有氧能力的指標。試說明限制 VO₂max 的兩項生理因素，並指出為何兩名 VO₂max 相同的跑手，長跑成績可以相差甚遠。
questionEn: Maximal oxygen uptake is commonly used as an index of aerobic capacity. State two physiological factors that limit it, and explain why two runners with the same value may differ greatly in distance-running performance.
explanation: 第二問是重點，考核考生知否 VO₂max 只是上限而非表現本身。答卷須提出至少一項 VO₂max 以外的決定因素。
explanationEn: The second part is the focus and tests whether the candidate knows that maximal oxygen uptake is a ceiling rather than performance itself. At least one further determinant must be offered.
referenceAnswer:
限制 VO₂max 的兩項因素：
一、中央因素——心輸出量。心輸出量等於心率乘每搏輸出量，決定每分鐘可送往工作肌的血液量。最大心率大致由年齡決定且難以訓練，故可訓練的主要是每搏輸出量（心室容積與收縮力）。對大多數人而言，這是最主要的限制。
二、周邊因素——肌肉攝取及利用氧的能力。包括肌肉的微血管密度、線粒體數目與體積，以及氧化酶的活性。此決定血液送到之後，氧能否被實際用於產生三磷酸腺苷。
（其他可接受：血液攜氧能力，即血紅蛋白濃度；肺部氣體交換能力，惟一般非健康者之限制因素。）
何以成績可以相差甚遠：
VO₂max 指的是「每分鐘最多能用多少氧」，屬上限；長跑成績則取決於「能夠在此上限的多高比例上維持多久，以及每一份氧能跑多遠」。至少三項因素獨立於 VO₂max：
一、乳酸閾值。指能長時間維持而血乳酸不急劇上升的強度，通常以 VO₂max 的百分比表示。甲跑手可在 85% 維持，乙跑手只能在 70%，即使兩者上限相同，實際比賽配速已相差甚遠。
二、跑步經濟性。指在同一速度下的耗氧量。技術、步頻、彈性能量回收與體重均影響此值。經濟性較佳者以較少的氧跑出同一速度，等於把同一個上限用得更遠。
三、耐熱能力、補給策略與比賽心理等實戰因素。
故 VO₂max 是必要條件，不是成績本身 —— 它決定「潛力的天花板」，而上述因素決定「實際能用到天花板的幾多」。
referenceAnswerEn:
Two limiting factors: first, the central factor of cardiac output, the product of heart rate and stroke volume, which sets how much blood reaches the working muscles each minute. Maximal heart rate is largely set by age and responds little to training, so what can be trained is chiefly stroke volume, through ventricular volume and contractility. For most people this is the principal limitation.
Second, the peripheral factor of the muscle's capacity to extract and use oxygen: capillary density, the number and size of mitochondria, and the activity of oxidative enzymes. This determines whether oxygen delivered can actually be used to make ATP.
(Also acceptable: the oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood, that is haemoglobin concentration; pulmonary gas exchange, though not usually limiting in the healthy.)
Why performance can differ greatly: maximal oxygen uptake is the most oxygen usable per minute — a ceiling. Distance performance depends on how high a fraction of that ceiling can be sustained and for how long, and on how far each unit of oxygen carries the runner. At least three factors are independent of the ceiling.
First, lactate threshold: the intensity that can be sustained without a sharp rise in blood lactate, usually expressed as a percentage of the maximum. A runner able to hold 85 per cent and one able to hold only 70 per cent will race at very different paces despite an identical ceiling.
Second, running economy: the oxygen cost of a given speed. Technique, cadence, elastic energy return and body mass all affect it, and a more economical runner covers the same speed on less oxygen, extending the same ceiling further.
Third, practical factors such as heat tolerance, fuelling strategy and race psychology.
Maximal oxygen uptake is therefore a necessary condition rather than performance itself: it sets the ceiling of potential, while the factors above determine how much of that ceiling is actually used.

subject: pe
question: 跳遠起跳時，運動員會把手臂與自由腿快速向上擺動。試以動量與地面反作用力解釋此一動作的作用。
questionEn: In the take-off for a long jump the athlete swings the arms and free leg upwards rapidly. Explain the effect of this action in terms of momentum and ground reaction force.
explanation: 本題須以力學原理作答，不可只說「幫助跳高啲」。答卷宜同時處理節段動量傳遞與地面反作用力兩條路徑。
explanationEn: The answer must use mechanical principles rather than say that it helps to jump higher, and should address both the transfer of segmental momentum and the ground reaction force.
referenceAnswer:
作用一：增加系統的垂直動量（節段動量傳遞）。
手臂與自由腿向上加速時，各自獲得向上的動量。當這些節段在接近起跳末段被主動減速（由肩關節與髖關節的肌肉制動），其動量依動量守恆傳遞至身體其餘部分，使整體重心的垂直速度增加。
關鍵在於【減速的時機】：必須在腳離地之前完成制動，動量才傳得到軀幹；若擺動持續至離地之後，該部分動量仍留在肢體本身，對重心無益。
作用二：增加地面反作用力。
要令手臂與自由腿向上加速，支撐腿必須施力於地面。依牛頓第三定律，地面對人體施以大小相等、方向相反的反作用力。故擺動愈快、被加速的質量愈大，起跳期間的垂直地面反作用力愈大。
衝量等於力乘時間，而衝量等於動量變化。在起跳時間極短（約 0.11 至 0.13 秒）且難以延長的情況下，唯一能增加垂直動量的途徑就是增大力 —— 擺臂與擺腿正是增大力的方法。
附帶作用：
手臂上擺亦有助於維持起跳時的身體姿態與平衡，並延遲騰空初期的前旋，使運動員有較充裕的時間在空中作出調整。
referenceAnswerEn:
First effect: it increases the vertical momentum of the system through the transfer of segmental momentum. As the arms and free leg accelerate upwards each gains upward momentum. When these segments are actively decelerated near the end of the take-off, braked by the muscles at the shoulder and hip, their momentum is transferred to the rest of the body by conservation of momentum, raising the vertical velocity of the whole centre of mass.
The timing of that braking is decisive: it must be completed before the foot leaves the ground for the momentum to reach the trunk. If the swing continues past take-off, that momentum stays in the limb and does nothing for the centre of mass.
Second effect: it increases the ground reaction force. To accelerate the arms and free leg upwards, the support leg must apply force to the ground, and by Newton's third law the ground applies an equal and opposite force to the body. The faster the swing and the greater the mass accelerated, the larger the vertical ground reaction force during take-off.
Impulse is force multiplied by time and equals the change in momentum. Since take-off lasts a very short time, roughly 0.11 to 0.13 seconds, and can hardly be lengthened, the only way to add vertical momentum is to raise the force — which is exactly what the arm and leg swing does.
A further effect: the upward arm swing helps to hold posture and balance at take-off and delays forward rotation in early flight, giving the athlete more time to adjust in the air.

subject: pe
question: 運動前後的補水常被簡化為「多飲水就得」。試指出此一說法的兩項不足，並說明長時間運動時補充電解質的理由。
questionEn: Hydration around exercise is often reduced to drinking plenty of water. State two shortcomings of that advice, and explain why electrolytes are needed during prolonged exercise.
explanation: 本題須指出過量飲用清水亦有風險，而非只談脫水。答卷宜提及低鈉血症與吸收速率兩個面向。
explanationEn: The answer must show that excessive plain water also carries risk rather than discuss dehydration only, and should cover hyponatraemia and the rate of absorption.
referenceAnswer:
不足一：忽略「飲得過多」同樣有害。
汗液中除水分外亦含鈉。長時間大量出汗後若只補充清水，體內鈉濃度被稀釋，可導致運動相關低鈉血症。症狀包括頭痛、噁心、意識混亂，嚴重者可致腦水腫。此情況在馬拉松等長時間項目中曾有記錄，而部分個案的成因正是「跟足指示不斷飲水」。
不足二：忽略時機與速率。
人體每小時能吸收的液體有限（大致每小時 0.6 至 1.2 公升，因人而異），而出汗率可能超出此數。故「感到口渴才飲」或「事後一次過大量補充」皆不理想：前者已落後於流失，後者超出吸收速率，多餘部分會以尿液排出或積在胃部造成不適。較佳做法是運動前已維持良好水分狀態，運動期間定時小量補充。
（其他可接受之不足：以口渴為唯一指標並不可靠，長者與兒童的口渴感較遲鈍；未考慮環境溫度與濕度。）
長時間運動補充電解質的理由：
一、維持血漿滲透壓與鈉濃度，直接預防上述低鈉血症。
二、鈉有助於水分的吸收與保留。小腸的葡萄糖—鈉共同轉運機制會把水一併帶入，故含適量鈉與糖的飲品，其水分吸收速率高於清水。
三、鈉與鉀參與神經傳導與肌肉收縮。濃度失衡與抽筋、乏力相關。
一般原則：運動少於一小時、強度中等者，清水已足夠；超過一小時、在高溫下進行、或出汗量大者，應補充含電解質的飲品。
referenceAnswerEn:
First shortcoming: it ignores the harm of drinking too much. Sweat contains sodium as well as water. After prolonged heavy sweating, replacing only plain water dilutes the body's sodium and can cause exercise-associated hyponatraemia, with headache, nausea and confusion, and in severe cases cerebral oedema. Cases have been recorded in marathons, and some arose precisely from following instructions to keep drinking.
Second shortcoming: it ignores timing and rate. The body can absorb only a limited volume per hour, broadly 0.6 to 1.2 litres depending on the individual, while sweat rate may exceed that. Drinking only when thirsty and drinking a large volume all at once afterwards are both poor: the first already lags behind the loss, and the second exceeds absorption, so the excess is passed as urine or sits in the stomach causing discomfort. Better practice is to be well hydrated before exercise and to take small amounts at regular intervals during it.
(Other acceptable shortcomings: thirst alone is an unreliable guide, and is blunted in the elderly and in children; ambient temperature and humidity are not considered.)
Why electrolytes are needed in prolonged exercise: they maintain plasma osmolality and sodium concentration, directly preventing the hyponatraemia described. Sodium also aids the absorption and retention of water, since the sodium-glucose co-transport mechanism in the small intestine carries water with it, so a drink containing suitable sodium and sugar is absorbed faster than plain water. Sodium and potassium also take part in nerve conduction and muscle contraction, and imbalance is associated with cramp and weakness.
As a general rule, plain water suffices for moderate exercise under an hour; beyond an hour, in heat, or with heavy sweating, an electrolyte drink should be used.

subject: pe
question: 訓練原則中的「超負荷」與「漸進」必須並用。試說明只有超負荷而無漸進、以及只有漸進而無超負荷，分別會出現甚麼問題。
questionEn: The principles of overload and progression must be applied together. Explain what goes wrong with overload but no progression, and with progression but no overload.
explanation: 本題以兩個反例考核原則之間的關係。答卷須就兩種情況分別作答，並指出各自的後果。
explanationEn: The question tests the relation between principles through two counter-cases, each of which must be answered separately with its own consequence.
referenceAnswer:
只有超負荷而無漸進：
所謂超負荷，指訓練刺激須超出身體目前所習慣的水平，方能引發適應。若一開始即施加遠高於現有能力的負荷而不逐步增加，身體的結構適應（肌腱、韌帶、骨骼）跟不上功能上的能力提升，容易出現過度使用性傷害。
另一種情況是：負荷雖高但長期維持不變。身體在數週內適應該水平之後，同一刺激不再構成超負荷，進步隨即停滯，形成平台期。訓練者往往誤以為需要「練得更辛苦」，實際需要的是改變負荷。
此外，高負荷而無恢復與遞增規劃，容易累積疲勞，導致表現下降甚至過度訓練症候群。
只有漸進而無超負荷：
若每次訓練的負荷都在身體的舒適範圍之內，即使負荷緩慢增加，亦未曾超出現有的適應水平，則不構成有效刺激。身體沒有理由作出改變 —— 適應是對「應付不來」的回應，不是對「應付得來」的回應。
結果是訓練量投入不少，體適能卻長期無明顯改善。此情況在自主訓練者中常見：因為感覺舒適，所以可以持續，但持續的是一種不產生適應的活動。
兩者的關係：
超負荷提供【方向】—— 必須超出現狀；漸進提供【速率】—— 超出多少、多快增加。缺前者無刺激，缺後者則刺激失控或凝固。二者須同時成立，訓練方能既有效又安全。
referenceAnswerEn:
Overload without progression: overload means the training stimulus must exceed what the body is currently accustomed to if adaptation is to follow. If a load far above present capacity is applied from the outset without stepwise increase, structural adaptation in tendon, ligament and bone lags behind the gain in functional capacity, and overuse injury readily follows.
A second case is a high load held unchanged for long. Once the body has adapted to that level within a few weeks, the same stimulus no longer constitutes overload, progress stalls and a plateau forms. Trainees often suppose they must work harder, when what is needed is a change of load.
High loads without planned recovery and increment also accumulate fatigue, leading to declining performance and even overtraining syndrome.
Progression without overload: if every session stays within the body's comfortable range, then even though the load rises slowly it has never exceeded the existing level of adaptation and constitutes no effective stimulus. The body has no reason to change, since adaptation is a response to what cannot yet be managed, not to what can.
The result is considerable training volume with no marked improvement in fitness over long periods. This is common among those training alone: because it feels comfortable it can be sustained, but what is sustained is activity that produces no adaptation.
The relation between them: overload supplies the direction — it must exceed the present state; progression supplies the rate — by how much and how quickly. Without the first there is no stimulus; without the second the stimulus is either uncontrolled or frozen. Both must hold for training to be effective and safe.

subject: pe
question: 一名 60 公斤的運動員以 12 km/h 的速度跑步 30 分鐘，該速度下每公斤體重每分鐘耗氧約 40 毫升。已知每公升氧約可釋放 5 千卡能量。試計算此節運動的總耗氧量與能量消耗，並指出此估算方法的兩項限制。
questionEn: A 60 kg athlete runs for 30 minutes at 12 km/h, at which speed oxygen consumption is about 40 ml per kilogram of body mass per minute. One litre of oxygen releases about 5 kcal. Calculate total oxygen consumption and energy expenditure for the session, and state two limitations of this method of estimation.
explanation: 本題須完整寫出單位換算步驟，只給最終數字不足。限制一問須針對此計算方法本身的假設。
explanationEn: The unit conversions must be written out in full; a final figure alone is not sufficient. The limitations must address the assumptions of this method of calculation.
referenceAnswer:
計算：
步驟一　每分鐘耗氧量
40 毫升／公斤／分鐘 × 60 公斤 = 2,400 毫升／分鐘 = 2.4 公升／分鐘
步驟二　總耗氧量
2.4 公升／分鐘 × 30 分鐘 = 72 公升
步驟三　能量消耗
72 公升 × 5 千卡／公升 = 360 千卡
答：總耗氧量約 72 公升，能量消耗約 360 千卡。
⚠️ 常見錯誤：漏了乘體重，直接以 40 × 30 = 1,200 作答。單位是【每公斤】，必須先乘體重才得出全身耗氧量。
估算方法的限制：
一、「每公升氧釋放 5 千卡」只是平均值。實際數值視乎所用燃料而定：完全氧化醣類時約為 5.05 千卡／公升，完全氧化脂肪時約為 4.69 千卡／公升。運動強度愈高，醣類比例愈大。以單一數值代入，會引入約 7% 的誤差，而該誤差的方向隨強度而變。
二、未計算運動後過量耗氧（EPOC）。運動結束後，身體仍需額外耗氧以回復體溫、補充磷酸肌酸、清除代謝物並恢復荷爾蒙水平。此部分能量消耗未計入，故 360 千卡是低估值。
（其他可接受之限制：40 毫升／公斤／分鐘 為該速度的典型值，個體的跑步經濟性差異可達 10% 以上；假設整節維持穩定狀態，但起跑初段尚未達到穩態；未扣除靜息代謝率，若目的是計算「額外」消耗，應減去同時段的靜息耗氧。）
referenceAnswerEn:
Calculation.
Step 1, oxygen consumption per minute: 40 ml per kg per min x 60 kg = 2,400 ml/min = 2.4 L/min.
Step 2, total oxygen consumption: 2.4 L/min x 30 min = 72 L.
Step 3, energy expenditure: 72 L x 5 kcal/L = 360 kcal.
Answer: about 72 litres of oxygen and about 360 kcal.
Common error: omitting body mass and computing 40 x 30 = 1,200. The unit is per kilogram, so body mass must be applied first to obtain whole-body consumption.
Limitations: first, 5 kcal per litre is an average. The true value depends on the fuel oxidised — about 5.05 kcal/L for carbohydrate and about 4.69 kcal/L for fat — and the proportion of carbohydrate rises with intensity. Using a single value introduces an error of roughly 7 per cent whose direction varies with intensity.
Second, excess post-exercise oxygen consumption is not counted. After exercise the body continues to use extra oxygen to restore temperature, replenish creatine phosphate, clear metabolites and restore hormonal balance. That energy is excluded, so 360 kcal is an underestimate.
(Other acceptable limitations: 40 ml/kg/min is a typical value for that speed, and individual running economy varies by more than 10 per cent; the calculation assumes steady state throughout, whereas the opening minutes have not reached it; resting metabolic rate has not been subtracted, and should be if the additional cost of exercise is what is wanted.)

subject: pe
question: 某中學欲提高學生的體能活動量，提出「每日午息強制全校跑步十五分鐘」。試從運動科學與學生動機兩方面評估此建議，並提出一項較可行的替代方案。
questionEn: A secondary school proposes fifteen minutes of compulsory running for all students during the lunch break, to raise physical activity levels. Evaluate the proposal in terms of exercise science and of student motivation, and propose a more workable alternative.
explanation: 本題為政策評估。答卷須分兩個角度評估並提出替代方案，三部分缺一不可。替代方案須針對已指出的問題。
explanationEn: This is a policy evaluation with three required parts: two angles of assessment and an alternative, which must address the problems identified.
referenceAnswer:
運動科學方面：
可取之處：十五分鐘中等強度活動確實對心肺功能有益；每日進行亦符合世衞對青少年每日至少六十分鐘中等至劇烈活動的建議，可構成其中一部分。
問題：
一、強度未按個體調節。同一速度對體能較佳者屬輕鬆，對肥胖或體能較差者可能已接近最大強度，後者容易出現不適並產生恐懼。
二、缺乏熱身與緩和。午息時間有限，學生由靜坐狀態直接開跑，肌肉溫度未升，受傷風險上升；跑畢即回課室亦不利恢復。
三、單一模式。只跑步無法涵蓋肌力、柔軟度與骨骼健康所需的負重多樣性；亦不照顧有哮喘、關節問題或殘疾的學生。
四、飯後時段未必適宜劇烈活動。
學生動機方面：
一、強制會削弱內在動機。自我決定理論指出，自主感是持續參與的關鍵。把活動變成義務，會把原本可能出於興趣的參與，轉為履行規定；規定一旦解除，行為多數隨即停止。
二、公開的能力比較。全校同時跑步，體能較差的學生在同儕面前落後，容易引發尷尬與逃避。研究普遍指出，負面的體育經驗與成年後的不活躍有關 —— 即長遠效果可能與目標相反。
三、佔用午息。午息亦是學生的社交與休息時間，剝奪之會引起抵觸，並把「運動」與「損失」連結起來。
較可行的替代方案：
設立多選項的午間活動時段：提供跑步、球類、跳繩、舞蹈、健身操等若干選擇，學生自選其一，每週要求參與三至四次而非每日強制。
此方案針對上述問題：提供選擇以保留自主感；不同項目的強度與技術要求不同，體能較差者可選擇壓力較小的項目，避免公開比較；保留部分午息作休息，減少抵觸；亦可按天氣與場地彈性調整。
配套：以參與紀錄而非表現排名作為追蹤；教師示範參與；並為有健康狀況的學生提供適應性選項。
referenceAnswerEn:
Exercise science: what is sound — fifteen minutes of moderate activity does benefit cardiorespiratory fitness, and doing it daily contributes towards the WHO recommendation of at least sixty minutes of moderate to vigorous activity a day for adolescents.
Problems: intensity is not individualised, so the same pace is easy for the fitter and close to maximal for students who are obese or unfit, who may feel unwell and become fearful. There is no warm-up or cool-down: with a short lunch break, students go from sitting straight into running with cold muscles and raised injury risk, and return to class without recovery. The single mode of activity does not provide the loading variety needed for strength, flexibility and bone health, and does not accommodate students with asthma, joint problems or disability. Vigorous activity soon after eating is also not ideal.
Student motivation: compulsion undermines intrinsic motivation. Self-determination theory holds that a sense of autonomy is central to sustained participation; making activity an obligation converts what might have been interest into compliance, and behaviour usually stops once the requirement is lifted. Running as a whole school also makes competence publicly comparable, so less fit students fall behind in front of their peers, inviting embarrassment and avoidance; negative experiences in physical education are generally associated with inactivity in adulthood, so the long-run effect may be the opposite of what is intended. Taking the lunch break also removes students' time for socialising and rest, which breeds resistance and links exercise with loss.
A more workable alternative: a lunchtime activity period with several options — running, ball games, skipping, dance, fitness classes — from which students choose, with participation expected three or four times a week rather than compulsory daily.
This addresses the problems: choice preserves autonomy; different activities vary in intensity and technical demand, so less fit students can choose lower-pressure options and avoid public comparison; part of the break is left for rest, reducing resistance; and the programme can flex with weather and facilities.
Supporting measures: track participation rather than ranking performance; have teachers take part; and provide adapted options for students with health conditions.
